text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming_route latency breach in shared-gpu-pool (us-west-2). p99 = 1.45s (SLO 1.0s). Increased streaming stalls observed. Grafana: https://grafana.company/r/alerts/6321

incident-bot: Affected services: streaming_route (multi-tenant model serving). Top symptom: high tail latency and intermittent stalls during token streaming. Related metrics: nvme_iops spike, cgroup writeback backlog.

maria: oncall here, ack. I'll pull logs and check cgroups on the affected hosts. @jon please open a host-level view for the top noisy hosts.

jon: looking. Querying Prometheus for per-host p99 and nvme write latency. PromQL I ran:

```
max by (host) (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/streaming"}[5m])) by (le,host)))
```

jon: host gpu-uw2-23 and gpu-uw2-27 show p99 > 1.2s and NVMe write_latency spiking to 30-60ms. cgroup blkio write backlog looks high.

kevin: sounds like noisy neighbor causing IO contention in shared pool. Any tenant with large batch writes or checkpointing?

maria: checking tenant mapping. Found tenant ids: t-acmecorp and t-bench-alpha with high write rates on gpu-uw2-23.

anita: FYI, AcmeCorp is on Dedicated? I thought they were on reserved capacity. If they are on shared pool that could be bad for SLA.

maria: AcmeCorp appears to be on shared-gpu-pool for a subset of models (weird routing policy fallback). I'll verify.

jon: I can throttle blkio for the noisy cgroup as a quick mitigation. Plan: set cgroup blkio.weight for tenant cgroup to lower value, and enable immediate eviction of background write tasks.

kevin: +1. Also prepare route fallback to dedicated-small pool for affected customers to reduce impact on streaming latency. We can flip routing in the loadbalancer for t-acmecorp.

maria: executing mitigation now. First, limiting blkio weight:

```
echo 100 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenant-t-acmecorp/blkio.weight
```

maria: applied to tenant-t-acmecorp on gpu-uw2-23. Monitoring latency...

ops-bot: Action recorded: cgroup blkio.weight update by maria (runbook: noisy-neighbor-mitigation).

jon: I also put an eviction on background write queues:

```
echo 1 > /sys/fs/cgroup/tenant-t-acmecorp/force_write_eviction
```

jon: eviction triggered, background IO reduced. p99 on gpu-uw2-23 dropped from 1.45s -> 0.9s (next scrape).

maria: good. Starting partial drain of t-acmecorp routing to dedicated-small for streaming_route: update in-progress on routing layer.

kevin: route flip in progress: `curl -X POST https://router/api/route/switch -d '{"tenant":"t-acmecorp","route":"dedicated-small"}'` (will wait for canary).

maria: canary passed on 2 hosts, flipping rest now.

anita: I'm messaging AcmeCorp CS lead that we're mitigating and may be routed to dedicated nodes — asking for tolerance for short interruption.

anita: message sent to AcmeCorp: "We detected transient streaming latency and have rerouted your streaming traffic to dedicated capacity to restore SLOs. No data loss expected. We'll follow up with details."

jon: monitoring shows global p99 for streaming_route is trending down to 0.85s. NVMe write_latency also dropping.

maria: verifying customer impact: preliminary: ~2.1% of streaming requests saw >1s extra tail latency over last 20m. Affected tenants: t-acmecorp (majority), t-bench-alpha (minor). No error spikes or request failures.

kevin: good. I'll keep the route fallback for 1 hour while we stabilize and then run a controlled rollback. Also want to schedule a host eviction of t-bench-alpha for aggressive background IO.

jon: logging actions in incident tracker. Creating short timeline:
- 6210009876 incident alert triggered (p99 1.45s)
- 6210009888 cgroup weight reduced for t-acmecorp on gpu-uw2-23
- 6210009905 background write eviction triggered
- 6210009918 routing canary to dedicated-small

maria: capturing debugging artifacts:
```
# top IO processes on gpu-uw2-23
ps aux --sort=-%io | head -n 20
# dstat snapshot
dstat -cdlmn --output /tmp/dstat-6210009876.csv 5 12
```

maria: uploading logs to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/6210009876/

ops-bot: Incident updates saved to incident-6210009876. Owner assigned: maria. Severity: Sev2.

anita: CS note: AcmeCorp confirmed improved latency after reroute and appreciates proactive routing change. They asked for a postmortem and whether reserved routing can be enforced so they aren't on shared pool in future.

kevin: note: model routing policy bug — fallback to shared pool happened because dedicated-small pool reached burst capacity and fallback policy allowed cross-tenant placement. Adding action to tighten fallback policy and add tenant-affinity for account with contract.

jon: next steps (short):
- [maria] collect host-level IO traces and attach to postmortem (24h).
- [kevin] patch routing config to prefer tenant-affinity for reserved customers (PR + canary, 48h).
- [infra] evaluate adding IO QoS enforcement at hypervisor level, not just cgroup (72h).

maria: marking incident as mitigated — p99 restored and streaming stalls cleared. Will keep monitoring for 30m before closing.

anita: I'll set up a follow-up customer call with AcmeCorp and include product/eng.

dave: quick question: do we want to retroactively credit AcmeCorp for the partial SLO window? We should calc exposure and escalate for billing ops.

maria: capture telemetry and we'll compute exposure. If >1% of requests and SLA breach timeframe >5m, escalate to Billing.

jon: closing notes: suspect root cause = aggressive background checkpointing from t-acmecorp combined with fallback routing to shared pool under burst conditions, amplifying NVMe write pressure and cgroup writeback backlog which increased tail latency for streaming.

maria: created postmortem draft: https://docs.company/postmortems/6210009876-draft (ownership: maria, kevin, jon).

ops-bot: Incident mitigated. Current status: degraded -> mitigated. Monitoring window open for 30m.

maria: thumbs. I'll update this thread with final numbers and then close. :white_check_mark:
